mainTopic: Abnormal eating, combining food and drink, and the source of the אזהרה for not fasting on יום כיפור
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a זר who chews raw barley of תרומה pays the קרן but not the חומש, because harmful eating is not real 'eating'. רבי יוחנן then rules on plums of תרומה that were swallowed, vomited, and eaten by someone else. Next the גמרא asks why eating and drinking do not combine on יום כיפור. רב חסדא and ריש לקיש say the משנה follows רבי יהושע's rule from הלכות טומאה. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say even the רבנן agree, because the יום כיפור measure depends on יתובי דעתא. A new משנה teaches that eating and drinking bring one חטאת, eating and מלאכה bring two, and unfit food or brine is exempt. The גמרא then searches for the Torah's אזהרה against eating on יום כיפור. After ריש לקיש's explanation runs into a קשיא, a ברייתא and רבינא find it through a גזירה שוה of 'עצם' and 'עצם' with מלאכה, and רבי ישמעאל's school and רב אחא בר יעקב give other sources. רב פפא begins yet another source, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Chewing raw barley of תרומה is not real eating
steps.stepSummary: A זר who chews raw barley of תרומה pays the קרן but not the חומש. This is because 'כי יאכל' excludes someone who harms himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A non-כהן] who chews raw barley of תרומה pays back the principal, but he does not pay the extra fifth. The פסוק says 'if he eats', and that excludes someone who harms himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that it began earlier. The ברייתא teaches that chewing raw barley does not count as halachic 'eating'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a זר who eats תרומה by mistake pays the קרן plus a חומש. Here he still owes the קרן, because he destroyed property belonging to the כהן. But he does not owe the חומש, since that penalty applies only to normal 'eating', and chewing raw barley counts as harming himself. This backs up the idea that eating food in an unfit, harmful way is not real אכילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Chewing raw, unprocessed grain
The portion of produce given to a כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it
The principal, meaning the basic value of what was eaten
An extra fifth paid as a penalty by a זר who eats תרומה
One who harms or damages (here, he harms himself)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he pays nothing. He still pays the קרן, because he destroyed property that belongs to the כהן. Only the חומש, which is tied to real 'eating', is dropped.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets the rule that harmful or abnormal consumption does not count as 'eating'. That same principle applies to the איסור of eating on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: who chews raw barley of terumah —
phrases.notes: This continues the ברייתא begun on the previous amud. The subject is a זר (non-כהן).

phrases.english: pays the principal
but does not pay the fifth.
"If he eats" — this excludes one who harms himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that was cited in the previous section of the daf
steps.raayaObject: That eating something in a harmful, unfit way is not halachic אכילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a זר chewing raw barley of תרומה, based on the פסוק 'כי יאכל'

steps.title: Plums of תרומה swallowed, vomited, and eaten by another
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules on plums of תרומה swallowed whole and vomited out by a זר and then eaten by someone else. The first person pays קרן and חומש. The second pays the first only the value of the plums as fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A non-כהן swallowed plums of תרומה, vomited them out, and then another person ate them. The first person pays the principal and the fifth. The second person pays only the value of firewood, and he pays it to the first person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is quoted about two people who consumed the same plums of תרומה. One swallowed them and vomited them out, and the other then ate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swallowing plums whole still counts as eating, since he benefited from them. So the first person owes the full קרן and חומש, and by paying he effectively acquires the plums. Once vomited, the plums are disgusting and worth only as fuel. So the second person merely damaged the first person's 'firewood' and pays him that small value.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
A type of plum or small fruit
He vomited them out
The value of firewood, meaning their worth only as fuel

steps.confusionAlert: The second person pays the first person, not the כהן. The first person already paid the כהן in full and so owns the plums.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A non-priest who swallowed plums of terumah
and vomited them out, and another person ate them —
the first one pays the principal and the fifth.
The second one pays nothing except
the value of firewood, to the first one only.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case of abnormal eating of תרומה and its payment rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first swallower pays קרן and חומש. The second eater pays the first only the plums' value as fuel.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that eating and drinking don't combine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that eating and drinking do not combine on יום כיפור, and asks which תנא holds this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Eating and drinking do not combine.' Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור you are liable for eating a כותבת of food or drinking a מלא לוגמיו of liquid. The משנה says half of each does not add up to liability. The גמרא wants to know which תנא's reasoning produces this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They combine, meaning they add together to reach the required amount
Who is the תנא? (asking whose opinion a teaching follows)

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] Eating and drinking do not combine.
Who is the tanna [who taught this]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the משנה's rule about combining eating and drinking
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא behind the rule that eating and drinking do not combine

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is a dispute, and this follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that this question is a מחלוקת, and the משנה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is taught as a dispute, and the משנה is following רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the 'who is the תנא' question. The proof for his answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא admits that not everyone agrees with the משנה's rule; there is a מחלוקת. He places the משנה with רבי יהושע, whose general rule about combining appears in another משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught as a dispute
It follows the opinion of רבי יהושע

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
It is taught as a dispute,
and [our משנה] is following Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהושע, in a matter that is disputed

steps.title: רבי יהושע's rule: same impurity and same measure combine
steps.stepSummary: Proof from another משנה: רבי יהושע taught that items with the same type of טומאה and the same שיעור combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהושע stated a general rule. Anything whose טומאה and whose שיעור are the same combines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב חסדא's claim: רבי יהושע's general rule from הלכות טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For two half-pieces to add up, רבי יהושע requires them to match in two ways. They must have the same kind of טומאה, and the same minimum size (שיעור) to cause טומאה. For example, two half-כזיתים of נבילה combine.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A general rule
Its type of ritual impurity
Its minimum measure

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehoshua stated a general rule:
Anything whose impurity and whose measure are the same —
combines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב חסדא's answer
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע requires full sameness for items to combine
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבי יהושע's כלל about combining items for טומאה

steps.title: If impurity or measure differ, there is no combining
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע continues: if only the טומאה matches, or only the שיעור matches, or neither, the items do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the טומאה is the same but not the שיעור, or the שיעור is the same but not the טומאה, or neither is the same, they do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes רבי יהושע's rule by listing the cases where items do not combine. This completes the proof for our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Matching on only one of the two factors is not enough. Applied to יום כיפור: eating and drinking are both forbidden, but each has a different שיעור (a כותבת for food, a מלא לוגמיו for drink). So under רבי יהושע's logic they do not combine, exactly as our משנה rules.

keyTerms.meaning: But not
They do not combine

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, two things add up only if they match in both type and שיעור. Since food and drink have different שיעורים on יום כיפור, they do not combine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a principle from הלכות טומאה explains a rule about יום כיפור. It is a shared logic of combining that runs across different areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: [Same] impurity but not measure,
[same] measure but not impurity,
neither impurity nor measure —
they do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of רבי יהושע's rule begun in Step 5
steps.raayaObject: That things differing in שיעור, like food and drink, do not combine
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of רבי יהושע's כלל

steps.title: רב נחמן: Even the רבנן Can Agree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the משנה can follow the רבנן too, because their rule that different items combine applies only to טומאה, not to יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. The רבנן only said items combine there, regarding טומאה, because טומאה is one single concept. But here, on יום כיפור, the measure is about settling the mind, and this mix of eating and drinking does not settle the mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different answer to the question of step 3. He says we don't need to pin the משנה on רבי יהושע alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא assumed that if the רבנן combine different items for טומאה, they would combine food and drink on יום כיפור too. רב נחמן breaks that link: טומאה combines because it is one shared category, but the יום כיפור measure is based on יתובי דעתא, and food plus drink together does not reach that feeling of being settled.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the Rabbis
They only said that rule in that case, not beyond it
The single category of ritual impurity
Settling the mind: the feeling of being satisfied

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the רבנן were wrong about טומאה. He is saying their rule there does not carry over to יום כיפור, because the reason for the measure is different.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: You can even say it is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said there
regarding ritual impurity,
since impurity is one category.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, מִשּׁוּם יַתּוֹבֵי דַּעְתָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: But here, it is about settling the mind,
phrases.notes: The יום כיפור measure is set by when a person feels satisfied.

phrases.english: and this does not settle his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רב חסדא's answer by distinguishing טומאה from יום כיפור
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that eating and drinking do not combine
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even the רבנן, since יום כיפור depends on יתובי דעתא and not on a shared category

steps.title: ריש לקיש Agrees with רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says, like רב חסדא, that this is a מחלוקת and the משנה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said ריש לקיש: This is taught as a dispute, and the משנה is רבי יהושע, as we learned: רבי יהושע stated a general rule, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש held the same view as רב חסדא from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. The גמרא adds a second אמורא who reads the משנה the same way, using the same source: רבי יהושע's rule about combining.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said: another sage holds the same view
It is taught as a dispute

phrases.english: And so said Reish Lakish:
It is taught as a dispute,
and it is Rabbi Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: as we learned: Rabbi Yehoshua stated a general rule, etc.
phrases.notes: Refers to the source quoted in steps 5 and 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב חסדא's view and adds ריש לקיש as support

steps.title: רבי יוחנן Holds Like רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives the same answer as רב נחמן: even the רבנן agree, because יום כיפור is about settling the mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it is the רבנן. The רבנן only said items combine there regarding טומאה. But here it is about settling his mind, and this does not settle his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as ריש לקיש matched רב חסדא, the גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן matched רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two sides are paired: רב חסדא and ריש לקיש say the משנה is רבי יהושע only. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say it fits everyone, because יתובי דעתא is a different kind of measure than טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבי יוחנן said: the opposing view
His mind

steps.whatToRemember: Two camps: רב חסדא and ריש לקיש say the משנה is only רבי יהושע. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say even the רבנן agree, since יום כיפור is measured by יתובי דעתא.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: You can even say it is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said there
regarding ritual impurity,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, מִשּׁוּם יַתּוֹבֵי דַּעְתֵּיהּ הוּא,
phrases.english: but here, it is about settling his mind,
and this does not settle his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pairs רבי יוחנן with רב נחמן, against ריש לקיש
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even the רבנן agree, because of יתובי דעתא

steps.title: One Sin-Offering or Two
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that eating and drinking in one lapse of awareness bring one חטאת, but eating and doing מלאכה bring two.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he ate and drank in one lapse of awareness, he brings only one חטאת. If he ate and did מלאכה, he brings two חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how many חטאות a person brings for sinning by mistake on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating and drinking both fall under the one prohibition of עינוי, so together they bring one חטאת. Doing מלאכה is a separate prohibition, so eating plus מלאכה brings two.

keyTerms.meaning: In one lapse of awareness, one mistaken period
Sin-offering brought for an accidental sin
Forbidden labor

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he ate and drank in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable to only one sin-offering.
If he ate and did labor,
he is liable to two sin-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating and drinking bring one חטאת; eating and מלאכה bring two

steps.title: Inedible Food and Undrinkable Liquids Are Exempt
steps.stepSummary: Eating food that is not fit to eat, or drinking unfit liquids or fish brine, is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate foods not fit for eating, or drank liquids not fit for drinking, or drank fish brine or pickling liquid, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It teaches that eating things that are not normal food does not count as breaking the fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is against normal eating and drinking that relieves the affliction. Unfit food and harsh brine are not normal eating, so there is no חיוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Not fit for eating
Fish brine
Briny liquid used for pickling fish
Exempt

phrases.english: If he ate foods that are not fit for eating,
or drank liquids not fit for drinking,
or drank fish brine or pickling brine,
he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with cases of exemption
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating unfit food or drinking brine on יום כיפור is exempt

steps.title: Why No Explicit Warning Against Eating
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks why the Torah never states an explicit אזהרה against not afflicting oneself on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: ריש לקיש said: Why was no warning stated about עינוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with ריש לקיש's question. He sets up an explanation that follows in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the Torah gives a warning (לאו) and separately a punishment. For עינוי the Torah only writes the punishment of כרת, so ריש לקיש asks why the warning is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: An explicit warning or prohibition in the Torah
Affliction: the יום כיפור fast

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not asking whether eating is forbidden. He knows it is. He is asking why the Torah did not write the prohibition in the usual way.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה אַזְהָרָה בְּעִינּוּי?
phrases.english: Why was no warning stated about affliction?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה אַזְהָרָה בְּעִינּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah has no explicit warning for עינוי

steps.title: Writing 'Do Not Eat' Would Mean an Olive-Bulk
steps.stepSummary: It was not possible to write a warning. Writing 'לא יאכל' would set the measure at a כזית, which is wrong for יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it was not possible. How could the Torah write it? If the Torah wrote 'it shall not be eaten,' eating means a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers his own question. He begins testing possible wordings to show that none of them work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everywhere in the Torah, the word for eating means a כזית. But the יום כיפור measure is a ככותבת, which is bigger. So the wording 'do not eat' would set the wrong amount.

keyTerms.meaning: How could it be written?
The Merciful One: the Torah
Olive-bulk, the usual measure for eating

phrases.english: Because it was not possible.
How could it be written?
Let the Torah write: 'It shall not be eaten'
eating means an olive-bulk!
phrases.notes: The יום כיפור measure is a large date-bulk, so this would be wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question and rejects the first possible wording
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No wording works; 'do not eat' would set a כזית measure

steps.title: Writing 'Do Not Be Afflicted' Would Mean the Opposite
steps.stepSummary: Writing 'לא תעונה' as a command would mean 'get up and eat,' the opposite of what is intended.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah wrote 'do not be afflicted,' that means 'get up and eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש rejects the second possible wording. This completes his proof that no direct warning could be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A command 'do not be afflicted' would tell a person to eat, the reverse of the law. So the Torah instead wrote only the punishment: a soul 'אשר לא תעונה' will be cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not be afflicted
Get up and eat
It implies

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah could not write a direct warning for עינוי. 'Do not eat' means a כזית, and 'do not be afflicted' means 'go eat.' So the Torah wrote only the punishment of כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the יום כיפור fast appears in the Torah only as a punishment, and it sets up the search for where the warning is learned.

phrases.english: Let the Torah write: 'Do not be afflicted'
that means: Get up and eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second possible wording and finishes ריש לקיש's answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Do not be afflicted' would mean the opposite, so no warning could be written

steps.title: רב הושעיא suggests another wording for the warning
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא challenges the claim that no warning could be written. He suggests the Torah could have said 'Guard yourself lest you not be afflicted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא objected: Let the Torah write, 'Guard yourself lest you not be afflicted'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא attacks the answer we just heard. That answer said there was no good way to write a warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13-14 said 'לא יאכל' gives the wrong measure, and 'לא תעונה' sounds like a command to eat. רב הושעיא offers a wording that avoids both problems. It keeps the word 'afflicted' but adds warning words in front.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it
Let the Merciful One (the Torah) write
Guard yourself lest. These are standard words that make something a prohibition.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya strongly objects to it:
Let the Merciful One write
'Guard yourself lest you not be afflicted'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that no warning could be phrased
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in steps 13-14 that the Torah had no way to write a warning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different wording exists that avoids both the כזית problem and the 'get up and eat' problem

steps.title: That wording would create too many prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'השמר', 'פן', and 'לא' are each a negative word. That would count as several לאוין instead of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there would be too many negative commandments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב הושעיא's suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that 'השמר', 'פן', and 'אל' or 'לא' each signal a לאו. Stacking three of them would suggest three separate prohibitions for one act of eating. That is not the intended law.

keyTerms.meaning: They would be many
Negative commandments (לאוין)

phrases.english: If so, there would be too many negative commandments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends steps 13-14 against רב הושעיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the proposed wording causes a new problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'השמר פן לא תעונה' would be a clean single warning
steps.terutzMaskana: It would count as multiple לאוין, so it cannot be used

steps.title: רב ביבי suggests 'Guard yourself in the מצוה of affliction'
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי offers a softer wording with only one 'השמר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי objected: Let the Torah write, 'Guard yourself in the מצוה of affliction'!
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא tries a different wording that avoids stacking negative words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes the 'too many לאוין' problem from step 16 because there is only one warning word. It is a new attempt to show a warning was possible after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of affliction (fasting)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye strongly objects to it:
Let the Merciful One write: 'Guard yourself in the מצוה of affliction'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New objection that avoids the flaw found in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no warning could be written
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single 'השמר' attached to the מצוה would be one warning

steps.title: 'Guard' on a positive מצוה stays a positive מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a rule. 'השמר' on a לאו makes a לאו, but 'השמר' on an עשה only makes an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a rule: 'Guard' said about a prohibition is a prohibition, and 'Guard' said about a positive מצוה is a positive מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב ביבי's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'מצות עינוי' is a positive command, adding 'השמר' to it would just strengthen the עשה. It would not create a לאו, so we still would have no אזהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment
A positive commandment

phrases.english: If so (the problem is):
'Guard' said about a prohibition is a prohibition,
'Guard' said about a positive מצוה is a positive מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against רב ביבי's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general rule of how 'השמר' works
steps.terutzMaskana: It would only be an עשה, not a לאו
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'השמר' always means a prohibition. It takes on the nature of whatever מצוה it is attached to.

steps.title: רב אשי suggests 'Do not stray from affliction'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proposes 'אל תסור מן העינוי', a single clear negative wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: Let the Torah write, 'Do not stray from affliction'!
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא offers a wording that seems to avoid every problem raised so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אל תסור' is one clear לאו. It does not set a כזית measure, does not sound like 'get up and eat,' and does not stack several לאוין. It also is not tied to an עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not stray (a negative command)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly objects to it:
Let it write: 'Do not stray from affliction'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third objection, built to avoid all earlier flaws
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no warning could be written
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אל תסור' is a single, clean לאו with none of the earlier problems

steps.title: The objection stands unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits רב אשי's question is difficult and leaves it unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concedes it has no answer to רב אשי. This closes the discussion of ריש לקיש's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that the Torah had no way to write a warning is left with an open hole. The search for where the אזהרה comes from continues: step 21 brings a תנא who works from the פסוקים, and steps 30-39 find the source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (the challenge remains unanswered)

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the cycle by conceding רב אשי's point
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explanation that the Torah could not write a warning is left unresolved
steps.whatToRemember: Three suggested wordings: רב הושעיא's (too many לאוין), רב ביבי's (only an עשה), and רב אשי's (no answer, so קשיא).

steps.title: A תנא brings a source from the verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a בריתא that works with the פסוק 'ועניתם את נפשותיכם וכל מלאכה לא תעשו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a תנא brings it from here: 'And you shall afflict your souls, and you shall do no manner of labor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new approach. A תנא will work from the פסוקים, and his בריתא follows in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts עינוי and the ban on מלאכה side by side. That pairing becomes the base for comparing the two. The בריתא first sets the limits of כרת for each of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא derives it from here
And you shall afflict your souls

phrases.english: And a Tanna brings it from here:
'And you shall afflict your souls,
and you shall do no manner of labor.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the open קשיא, the גמרא brings a תנא who works from the verses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The source discussion is based on the פסוק pairing עינוי with the ban on מלאכה

steps.title: Maybe there is כרת for working during the added time
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא raises a possibility: perhaps one is punished for doing מלאכה during the תוספת, the time added before יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he is punished for labor during the added time.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא suggests a possible mistake so it can correct it with a פסוק. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מצוה to add time onto יום כיפור (תוספת). The question is whether breaking the ban on מלאכה during that added time carries the same כרת as the day itself.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
The added time before or after יום כיפור
Punished

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא עָנוּשׁ עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה —
phrases.english: One might think he is punished for labor in the added time —

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהֵא עָנוּשׁ עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the בריתא's discussion with a possible mistaken view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there כרת for doing מלאכה during the תוספת?

steps.title: כרת for labor applies only on the day itself
steps.stepSummary: The words 'בעצם היום הזה' show that כרת for מלאכה applies only on the actual day, not in the תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And whatever soul does any labor on that very day.' On the day itself he is punished with כרת, but not for labor during the added time.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא answers its own question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בעצם היום' means the essence of the day, the actual day of יום כיפור. That phrase limits כרת to the day itself. The added time still has a מצוה, but it carries no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
On that very day
The day itself
Spiritual cutting off

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And whatever soul does any labor
on that very day' —

phrases.aramaic: עַל עִיצּוּמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: for the day itself he is punished with karet,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה.
phrases.english: but he is not punished with karet for labor in the added time.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְכׇל הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה כׇּל מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No כרת for מלאכה in the תוספת. 'בעצם היום' limits it to the day itself.

steps.title: Maybe eating in the added time is different
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests that even if מלאכה in the תוספת has no כרת, perhaps not fasting in the תוספת does.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think there is no כרת for labor in the added time, but there is כרת for not afflicting oneself in the added time.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא raises a second possibility, this time about עינוי. It sets up another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think עינוי is stricter than מלאכה, so the limit just learned for מלאכה might not carry over. The בריתא checks whether כרת for eating reaches into the added time.

keyTerms.meaning: The added time of fasting

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה,
phrases.english: One might think he is not punished with karet for labor in the added time,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יְהֵא עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת עִינּוּי —
phrases.english: but he is punished with karet for the added time of affliction —

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question from מלאכה to עינוי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there כרת for eating during the תוספת?

steps.title: כרת for not fasting applies only on the day itself
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about עינוי also says 'בעצם היום הזה'. So כרת for eating applies only on the actual day, not in the תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For whatever soul is not afflicted on that very day shall be cut off.' On the day itself he is punished with כרת, but not for the added time of affliction.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא answers with the פסוק about עינוי, which uses the same limiting words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים say 'בעצם היום הזה', so both are limited the same way. Eating during the תוספת is still wrong, but it does not carry the כרת punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall be cut off
Is not afflicted (does not fast)

phrases.english: The verse states:
'For whatever soul is not afflicted
on that very day shall be cut off.'

phrases.aramaic: עַל עִיצּוּמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: For the day itself he is punished with karet,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת עִינּוּי.
phrases.english: but he is not punished with karet for the added time of affliction.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּי כׇל הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא תְעוּנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No כרת for not fasting in the תוספת. 'בעצם היום' limits it to the day itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Both מלאכה and eating carry כרת only on the actual day of יום כיפור ('בעצם היום הזה'), not during the added תוספת time.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying there is 'no כרת' for the תוספת does not mean the תוספת is permitted. There is still a מצוה to add time. Only the כרת punishment is limited to the day itself.

steps.title: Maybe there is a warning for work in the added time
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests that even without כרת, doing מלאכה in the תוספת might still carry an אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: a person who does work in the added time is not punished with כרת, but he still has a warning (a לאו) against doing work in the added time.
steps.whatsHappening: We already learned that there is no כרת for מלאכה in the תוספת. Now the בריתא asks about a lower level: maybe there is still a לאו that brings מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah punishments come in levels. כרת is the heavy punishment, and an אזהרה (a לאו) brings מלקות. Ruling out כרת does not yet rule out a plain לאו, so the בריתא checks that level next.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishment. Here it means כרת.
Warned. Under a לאו, a negative commandment that brings מלקות.
The extra time added onto יום כיפור before it starts.

steps.confusionAlert: In this בריתא, 'עונש' means כרת and 'מוזהר / אזהרה' means a לאו with מלקות. Keep these two levels apart, or the whole passage will get confusing.

phrases.english: One might think: he is not included in the punishment (כרת),

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יְהֵא מוּזְהָר עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה —
phrases.english: but he is warned against work in the added time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves down one level, from כרת to אזהרה, for מלאכה in the תוספת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there at least a לאו (מלקות) for doing מלאכה during the תוספת?

steps.title: No warning for work in the added time
steps.stepSummary: The words 'בעצם היום הזה' limit the אזהרה for מלאכה to the actual day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And you shall do no work on that very day.' This teaches that he is warned only about the day itself. He is not warned about work in the added time.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא answers with the same words it used before, 'בעצם היום הזה'. This time it applies them to the warning, not just to כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'לא תעשו' is itself the לאו against work. Since 'בעצם היום הזה' is attached to it, the לאו covers only the real day. So the תוספת has neither כרת nor a לאו for מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches.' This phrase introduces the proof from the פסוק.
The very essence of the day, meaning the actual day itself.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And you shall do no manner of work
on that very day."

phrases.aramaic: עַל עִיצּוּמוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם הוּא מוּזְהָר,
phrases.english: About the day itself he is warned,
but he is not warned about work in the added time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no לאו for מלאכה in the תוספת, because the לאו is limited by 'בעצם היום הזה'.

steps.title: Maybe there is a warning for not fasting in the added time
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps there is no אזהרה for מלאכה in the תוספת, but there is one for not fasting in the תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: he is not warned about work in the added time, but he is warned about not fasting in the added time.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא now asks the same 'warning' question about עינוי (fasting) instead of מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This copies the pattern of steps 22-25, where כרת was first checked for מלאכה and then for eating. Now the warning level is being checked the same way: first מלאכה, then עינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Affliction. The מצוה to fast (not eat or drink) on יום כיפור.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא מוּזְהָר עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה,
phrases.english: One might think: he is not warned about work in the added time,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יְהֵא מוּזְהָר עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת עִינּוּי —
phrases.english: but he is warned about fasting in the added time.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא מוּזְהָר עַל תּוֹסֶפֶת מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the warning question from מלאכה over to עינוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a לאו for not fasting during the תוספת?

steps.title: Logic shows there is no warning for fasting in the added time
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר: מלאכה is the broader prohibition and has no אזהרה in the תוספת, so עינוי surely has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: work is forbidden on every שבת and יום טוב, and yet there is no warning about it in the added time. Fasting is not required on שבת or יום טוב, so surely there is no warning about it in the added time!
steps.whatsHappening: This time the בריתא does not use a verse. It answers with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלאכה applies on many holy days, which makes it the 'stronger' prohibition. עינוי applies only on יום כיפור, which makes it 'weaker'. If the stronger one has no אזהרה in the תוספת, the weaker one certainly has none.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is logical.' This phrase introduces a קל וחומר.
Applies, is in force.
Logic from the stronger case to the weaker case (or the other way).

phrases.english: And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מְלָאכָה שֶׁנּוֹהֶגֶת בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: If work, which applies on שבתות and יום טוב,
he is not warned about it (in the added time),

phrases.aramaic: עִינּוּי, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: then fasting, which does not apply on שבתות and יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא מוּזְהָר עָלָיו?!
phrases.english: is it not logical that he is not warned about it?!

steps.whatToRemember: In the תוספת there is no כרת and no לאו, for either מלאכה or eating. Only the actual day carries these punishments.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with logic built on the ruling of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no לאו for עינוי in the תוספת, learned by קל וחומר from מלאכה.

steps.title: Where is the warning for not fasting on the day itself?
steps.stepSummary: The Torah states כרת for not fasting but never states a לאו. Where is the אזהרה for the actual day?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the warning for fasting on the day itself, we have not learned it. Where does it come from?
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא turns to a new question. For מלאכה we have 'לא תעשו', a clear לאו. For fasting the Torah only gives a positive command and כרת. So where is the לאו?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that the Torah does not give a punishment unless it also gives a warning. Since עינוי has כרת, it needs an אזהרה somewhere. This question opens a new search for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning. The לאו that must come before a punishment.
From where? The question asking for a source.

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the larger search for the source of the אזהרה for eating on יום כיפור. The rest of the sugya tries several answers to it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַזְהָרָה לְעִינּוּי שֶׁל יוֹם עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: But the warning for fasting on the day itself
we have not learned. From where is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אַזְהָרָה לְעִינּוּי שֶׁל יוֹם עַצְמוֹ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ מִנַּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תוספת to the actual day, and opens a new question about the source of the לאו for עינוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the אזהרה for not fasting on יום כיפור itself.

steps.title: The punishment for work did not need to be written
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts by showing that כרת for מלאכה could be learned by קל וחומר from עינוי, so the verse stating it looks extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah did not need to say the punishment for work, because it could be learned from fasting: fasting does not apply on שבת and יום טוב and still has כרת. Work applies on שבת and יום טוב, so certainly it should have כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the answer. It shows that one verse, the כרת for מלאכה, seems unnecessary, so it can be used to teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic runs from עינוי to מלאכה. If the narrower מצוה‎ (עינוי) carries כרת, the broader prohibition (מלאכה) surely does. So when the Torah writes כרת for מלאכה, the verse is 'free' for a new lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It need not say.' The verse is extra.
Since it can be learned.
All the more so.

phrases.english: Let it not state the punishment for work,
since it can be learned from fasting:

is punished with כרת,
then work, which applies on שבתות and ימים טובים,
all the more so, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 30 by showing that the verse giving כרת for מלאכה is extra.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כרת verse for מלאכה can be learned by קל וחומר, so it is free to teach something else.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה gives fasting a warning like work
steps.stepSummary: The extra verse is used for a גזירה שוה: just as מלאכה has a warning before its punishment, so does עינוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why was it written? It is free to be used for a גזירה שוה: a punishment is stated for fasting, and a punishment is stated for work. Just as with work the Torah punishes only after it warns, so too with fasting it punishes only after it warns.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא finishes the answer. It uses the 'free' verse to link עינוי to מלאכה, so that עינוי also has an אזהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה normally needs a 'free' (מופנה) word, so that it cannot be argued against. Both verses use the same punishment language. Since מלאכה has a clear לאו before its כרת, the link shows that עינוי also has an אזהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Free.' A verse not needed for its plain meaning, so it is available for a דרשה.
Linking two laws through similar wording in the Torah.

keyTerms.term: לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר
keyTerms.meaning: The Torah does not punish without first warning.

phrases.english: Why was it stated?

phrases.aramaic: מוּפְנֶה לְהַקִּישׁ וְלָדוּן מִמֶּנּוּ גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה:
phrases.english: It is free, to compare and learn a גזירה שוה from it:
A punishment is stated for fasting,
and a punishment is stated for work.

phrases.aramaic: מָה מְלָאכָה — לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר,
phrases.english: Just as with work, He did not punish unless He warned,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עִינּוּי — לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר.
phrases.english: so too with fasting, He did not punish unless He warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר מוּפְנֶה לְהַקִּישׁ וְלָדוּן מִמֶּנּוּ גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the extra verse shown in step 31 to build the גזירה שוה.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an אזהרה for not fasting on יום כיפור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from the 'free' verse stating כרת for מלאכה.

steps.title: The logic can be refuted: work has exceptions, fasting does not
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר from עינוי to מלאכה fails, because מלאכה has exceptions (Temple service) while עינוי has none. So the verse is not extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what is special about fasting is that it has no exceptions. Can you say the same about work, which does have exceptions?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר of step 31. If the קל וחומר falls, the כרת verse for מלאכה is needed after all. Then it is not 'free', and the גזירה שוה collapses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עינוי applies to everyone with no exceptions, which makes it strict in one way. מלאכה is allowed in the בית המקדש on יום כיפור (the עבודה), so it is weaker in that way. Because of this, we cannot say מלאכה is 'all the more so' strict. The Torah had to state its כרת on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It can be refuted.' This phrase attacks a קל וחומר.
Has a permitted exception to its general prohibition.

steps.confusionAlert: This refutation does not say מלאכה is not a strict prohibition. It only shows that, because of its Temple exception, we cannot be sure it is 'stronger' than עינוי. So the קל וחומר breaks.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to find the אזהרה for עינוי through this גזירה שוה fails, because its קל וחומר can be refuted.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about fasting? It has no exception to its general rule.
Will you say the same about work, which has an exception to its general rule?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the קל וחומר of step 31, which the גזירה שוה of step 32 depends on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from עינוי to מלאכה, and with it the 'free' status of the verse that the גזירה שוה relies on.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מלאכה has a permitted exception (Temple service on יום כיפור) while עינוי has none, so מלאכה is not clearly the stricter one.

steps.title: Flip the direction: learn the punishment for not fasting from work
steps.stepSummary: Instead of learning מלאכה from עינוי, the גמרא learns the כרת of עינוי from מלאכה with a קל וחומר. That makes the עונש verse for עינוי look extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: the Torah did not need to state the punishment for not fasting, because it can be learned from work. Work has exceptions where it is allowed, and it still carries כרת. Not fasting has no exceptions, so it should certainly carry כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: After the last attempt was knocked down, the גמרא tries the same idea in the opposite direction. This sets up the next move: if the עינוי verse is extra, what is it used for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said the קל וחומר from עינוי to מלאכה fails, because מלאכה has exceptions (Temple service) and עינוי does not. That same difference now works in favor of going from מלאכה to עינוי. If the looser prohibition (מלאכה) gets כרת, the stricter one (עינוי) surely does too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected approach)
Punishment (here, כרת)
Which was permitted out of its general rule (it has exceptions)
All the more so

phrases.english: Rather: let the punishment for affliction not be stated,
phrases.notes: Meaning: the Torah would not have needed to write it.

phrases.english: since it can be learned from labor.
Just as labor, which has permitted exceptions from its general rule —
phrases.notes: For example, the Temple service on יום כפורים.

phrases.english: is punished with כרת,
affliction, which has no permitted exceptions from its general rule —
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לֹא יֵאָמֵר עוֹנֶשׁ בְּעִינּוּי, דְּגָמַר מִמְּלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the דחיה of step 33 by running the קל וחומר the other way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the direction of the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse giving כרת for מלאכה was the extra one, but that failed because מלאכה has exceptions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse giving כרת for עינוי is the extra one, since it can be learned from מלאכה.

steps.title: The extra verse teaches that not fasting also has a warning
steps.stepSummary: Since the עונש verse for עינוי is extra, it is free for a גזירה שוה. Just as מלאכה has both a punishment and a warning, so does עינוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why was it written? It is free, to be used for a גזירה שוה. Punishment is stated for not fasting, and punishment is stated for work. Just as for work the Torah gave a punishment and a warning, so too for not fasting it gave a punishment and a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the extra verse to produce the missing אזהרה for not fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse that is not needed for its own simple meaning is called מופנה, meaning free. A free verse can be used to link two topics. The shared word עונש connects עינוי to מלאכה, so the אזהרה that מלאכה has carries over to עינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Free or available (a verse not needed for its plain meaning)
To compare and derive
Punished and warned (gave both a punishment and a לאו)

steps.confusionAlert: This is almost the same move as step 32, but the direction is flipped. Now the extra verse is the עונש of עינוי, not the עונש of מלאכה.

phrases.english: Why was it stated?

phrases.aramaic: מוּפְנֶה, לְהַקִּישׁ וְלָדוּן מִמֶּנּוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה:
phrases.english: It is free, to compare and derive from it a verbal analogy:
Punishment is stated regarding affliction,
and punishment is stated regarding labor;
just as for labor, He punished and warned —
so too for affliction, He punished and warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר — מוּפְנֶה, לְהַקִּישׁ וְלָדוּן מִמֶּנּוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the extra verse identified in step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an אזהרה for not fasting on יום כפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה built on the word עונש, which appears for both עינוי and מלאכה.

steps.title: Rejected: work is stricter because it applies on שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר of step 34 can be refuted. מלאכה is forbidden on every שבת and יום טוב, while עינוי applies only on יום כפורים. So מלאכה is stricter in that way, and we cannot learn the כרת of עינוי from it. That means the עונש verse for עינוי is needed after all, and it is not free for a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted. Work applies on שבתות and ימים טובים. Can you say the same about not fasting, which does not apply on שבתות and ימים טובים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reversed קל וחומר of step 34 by showing a way in which מלאכה is stricter than עינוי. Without that קל וחומר, the verse is not free, and the גזירה שוה of step 35 falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 said עינוי is stricter than מלאכה, so its כרת could be learned from מלאכה and its verse would be extra. But מלאכה is stricter in another way: it applies on every שבת and יום טוב, so the קל וחומר fails and the עינוי verse is needed for its own כרת. Without a free (מופנה) verse, the גזירה שוה falls, just as step 33 broke steps 31-32.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute
What about X? It has this strictness (standard challenge formula)
Applies, is in force

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not attacking the גזירה שוה head-on. It attacks the קל וחומר that made the verse 'free'. If the verse is not free, a logical difference between the two topics can knock down the comparison. Steps 38-39 deal with exactly this.

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about labor? It applies
on Shabbatot and Festivals.
Will you say the same of affliction, which does not apply
on Shabbatot and Festivals?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לִמְלָאכָה — שֶׁכֵּן נוֹהֶגֶת בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 34, which takes away the 'free' status that the גזירה שוה of step 35 relies on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from מלאכה to עינוי (step 34), and with it the free status of the עונש verse that the גזירה שוה of step 35 relies on.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מלאכה is stricter in that it applies on שבת and יום טוב, so the קל וחומר giving עינוי כרת from מלאכה fails. The עונש verse for עינוי is therefore needed, and it is not מופנה.

steps.title: רבינא: the source is the shared word "עצם"
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the תנא actually learned from the word עצם ("that very day"), which appears for both עינוי and מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This תנא learned it from "עצם" and "עצם."
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different link between the two topics, the repeated phrase בעצם היום הזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה is no longer based on the word עונש. It is based on the phrase עצם, which appears both in the verse about not fasting and in the verse about work (ויקרא כ״ג). This new link sets up the question in the next step: is it really free?

keyTerms.meaning: Very, essence (from בְּעֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה, "on that very day")
The author of the ברייתא
He derived

phrases.english: Ravina said:
This tanna derived it from "same" and "same."
phrases.notes: בעצם היום הזה appears in ויקרא כ״ג for both עינוי and מלאכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected עונש-to-עונש link with an עצם-to-עצם link.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting which words the גזירה שוה uses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא learned from the word עונש, which can be refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא learned from the word עצם.

steps.title: The word must be extra, or the same challenge returns
steps.stepSummary: This גזירה שוה only works if the word is free. Otherwise the earlier challenge about שבת and יום טוב would defeat it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be free, because if it were not free, it could be refuted the way we refuted it before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a condition for רבינא's answer: the word must be extra. This sets up the next step, which proves that it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה from a fully free word cannot be knocked down by logical differences. If the word is not free, the challenge from step 36 still works. So the real question is whether the עצם verses are truly extra.

keyTerms.meaning: For if not
As we refuted (earlier)

phrases.english: It must be free, for if it were not free —
it could be refuted as we refuted it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֶה, דְּאִי לָא מוּפְנֶה — אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ כִּדְפָרְכִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the condition that רבינא's גזירה שוה must meet.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the word עצם truly free (מופנה), so that it cannot be refuted?

steps.title: Five verses about work: one is free for the comparison
steps.stepSummary: Yes, it is free. The Torah has five verses about מלאכה on יום כפורים. Four teach the warning and punishment for day and night, and the fifth is free to teach עינוי, for both day and night.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is certainly free. Five verses are written about work: one for the warning by day, one for the warning by night, one for the punishment by day, one for the punishment by night, and one left free to learn not fasting from work, both by day and by night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the word is extra by counting the verses about מלאכה and finding one left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four verses cover everything מלאכה itself needs: a warning and a punishment, each for the day and for the night. The fifth verse has no job of its own, so it is truly free. Because it is free, the גזירה שוה cannot be refuted, and it gives עינוי an אזהרה for both the day and the night of יום כפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: No (it is not as you feared)
It is certainly free
Five verses
Of the day / of the night

steps.whatToRemember: The אזהרה for not fasting on יום כפורים comes from a גזירה שוה of עצם and עצם with מלאכה. It holds up because one of the five verses about מלאכה is extra, and it covers both the day and the night.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finally answers the question from step 30. Not fasting on יום כפורים has a real לאו, not only כרת.

phrases.english: No, it is certainly free.
Five verses are written about labor:
one for the warning by day,
and one for the warning by night,
and one for the punishment by day,
and one for the punishment by night,
and one left free to derive affliction from labor,
both by day and by night.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאיֵי, אִפְּנוֹיֵי מוּפְנֶה. חַמְשָׁה קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי בִּמְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 38 by showing that the verse is truly free.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are five verses about מלאכה. Four are needed for its own warning and punishment, day and night, and the fifth is free for the גזירה שוה to עינוי, both day and night.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עינוי on יום כפורים has an אזהרה, learned through an unrefutable גזירה שוה of עצם and עצם with מלאכה.

steps.title: Learning the warning from the word affliction in another place
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל's school compares עינוי on יום כפורים with עינוי in the case of a forced woman. There the Torah only punished after warning, so here too there must be a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The word 'affliction' is said here (about יום כפורים), and the word 'affliction' is said elsewhere (about a man who afflicted his neighbor's wife). Just as there, the Torah did not punish unless it first warned, so too here, the Torah did not punish unless it first warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way to prove that eating on יום כפורים has a Torah warning. It uses a word match (גזירה שוה) on the word עינוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עינוי appears for יום כפורים and also in the verse about a man who forced a betrothed woman ('על דבר אשר ענה את אשת רעהו'). In that case, the Torah gives a punishment only together with a warning. The גזירה שוה carries this pattern over to יום כפורים, so the punishment of כרת for not fasting must also come with a warning.

keyTerms.meaning: Affliction. On יום כפורים it means fasting. In the other verse it describes a man forcing himself on a woman.
'It says here... and it says there.' This is the standard way to open a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.term: לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר
keyTerms.meaning: The Torah does not give a punishment unless it first gave a warning.
Taught. This introduces a teaching from the time of the תנאים.

steps.confusionAlert: The word עינוי means two very different things in the two verses: fasting on יום כפורים and forcing a woman. A גזירה שוה works on the shared word, not on similar meaning. The cases do not need to resemble each other.

phrases.english: 'Affliction' is stated here (Yom Kippur),
and 'affliction' is stated there (the forced woman, Devarim 22:24).
phrases.notes: The verse is 'על דבר אשר ענה את אשת רעהו'.

phrases.english: Just as there, it did not punish
unless it had warned,
so too here, it did not punish
unless it had warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן עִינּוּי, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן עִינּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the עצם derivation was confirmed to be free, the גמרא offers another way to learn the same warning.
steps.raayaObject: There is a Torah warning (אזהרה) against eating on יום כפורים, not only a punishment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from the word עינוי, which appears for יום כפורים and for the forced woman in דברים 22:24.

steps.title: Learning the warning from the phrase שבת שבתון
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב compares the phrase שבת שבתון on יום כפורים with the same phrase about the weekly שבת. On שבת there is a warning before the punishment, so on יום כפורים there must be one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Learn 'שבת שבתון' (said about יום כפורים) from the שבת of Creation (the weekly שבת, where the same words appear). Just as there, the Torah did not punish unless it first warned, so too here, the Torah did not punish unless it first warned.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a third way to find the warning. He uses a word match on the phrase שבת שבתון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls יום כפורים 'שבת שבתון', and it uses the same phrase for the weekly שבת. On שבת, the punishment for working comes with a clear warning. Through the shared phrase, the same structure applies to יום כפורים, so its punishment also needs a warning.

keyTerms.meaning: A Shabbat of complete rest. This phrase is used for both יום כפורים and the weekly שבת.
The Shabbat of Creation, meaning the regular weekly שבת.
Learn or derive one thing from another.

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא now has several independent sources for the same warning. This shows how strongly the Torah's principle 'no punishment without warning' shapes the search for sources.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Derive 'Shabbat of solemn rest' (Yom Kippur)
from the Shabbat of Creation:
Just as there, it did not punish
unless it had warned,
so too here, it did not punish
unless it had warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: יָלֵיף שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן מִשַּׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another alternative source for the same warning, using a different shared phrase.
steps.raayaObject: There is a Torah warning against eating on יום כפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from the phrase שבת שבתון, used both for יום כפורים (ויקרא 16:31) and for the weekly שבת.

steps.title: רב פפא begins another approach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב פפא, who will offer yet another source. His actual words continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is introducing רב פפא, whose explanation comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attribution line is listed here only so that every word of the text is covered. It belongs to the statement that follows and does not stand alone. Expect רב פפא to give his own source for the warning.
